body:
## Summary

Fixes #2331. The onboard AICore objects are built by `add_custom_command` with
`DEPENDS ${SRC_FILE}` — only the `.cpp`. A header-only edit therefore left every
object byte-identical **and the build reported success**, so an A/B over a
platform header ran the same binary in both arms and reported no difference.

That is not hypothetical: #2233's fix measured **18/20 vs 17/20** this way — "the
fix does nothing" — from two arms that were one binary. The same change measured
0/20 after `rm -rf build/cache/a2a3/onboard`, three times.

`ccec` is clang 15 and reports what each object read, so this passes
`-MD -MF <obj>.d` and consumes it with `DEPFILE` instead of maintaining a header
list by hand. Each object now tracks the **30 repo-owned headers it actually
includes** (218 including CANN's), which answers the issue's open question — the
gap was never specific to `inner_kernel.h`, and a hand-written `DEPENDS` list
would have had to enumerate all 30 correctly per source per arch.

Two smaller things in the same pass:

- **`cmake_minimum_required` 3.16.3 → 3.20** in these two files, **and the
  advertised prerequisite moves to match** (15 places: `pyproject.toml`'s
  build-system requires, `docs/getting-started.md`, `docs/python-packaging.md`, and
  the ten workflows that pip-install a cmake floor). `DEPFILE` on the Makefile
  generators this project configures with needs 3.20. That advertisement was
  **already stale before this change** — it said 3.15 while 28 `CMakeLists.txt` in
  the tree declare 3.16.3 and 17 declare 3.16, so cmake 3.15 could not configure
  the repo either. The honest floor is the maximum any configured subproject needs.
  Below it, cmake fails the configure with its own message rather than silently
  producing stale objects. (Raised by CodeRabbit on this PR; its suggested
  alternative — drop `DEPFILE` but keep consuming ccec's depfile — is not
  possible, since `DEPFILE` is the mechanism that consumes it.)
- **`CONFIGURE_DEPENDS` on the source glob.** Same failure mode one level up: a
  newly added `.cpp` was not compiled until something else forced a reconfigure.
  Flagging it explicitly rather than burying it — it is one keyword, in the same
  file, with the same silent-staleness shape as the bug being fixed.

Not touched: the **sim** AICore builds use `add_library`, so cmake already tracks
their headers, and the AICPU CMakeLists use normal targets. Only these two files
have the gap.

No doc change needed. `docs/developer-guide.md`'s rebuild table already claims a
`src/{arch}/platform/` change is picked up incrementally — the doc was right and
the build was wrong.

## Testing

Verified per arch by md5 of `aicore_kernel.o`, **without wiping the cache** — the
exact scenario from the issue:

| step | a2a3 | a5 |
| ---- | ---- | -- |
| clean build | `b9ba5d90` | `76037e01` |
| header edit, incremental | `ca0e4eae` | `df4f99f3` |
| header reverted, incremental | `b9ba5d90` | `76037e01` |
| rebuild, no change | `b9ba5d90`, nothing recompiled | — |

- [x] `ca0e4eae` is **byte-identical to a from-scratch build** of that arm
      (measured independently in #2324's cost A/B), so the incremental result
      equals the clean one rather than merely differing
- [x] Tracks in both directions, not just "something changed once"
- [x] A no-change rebuild recompiles nothing (object mtime unchanged) — no
      spurious rebuild or reconfigure loop from `CONFIGURE_DEPENDS`
- [x] Depfiles are produced for all 7 objects per runtime and name
      `inner_kernel.h`
- [x] a5 onboard builds clean and shows the same behaviour

Before this change, every "header edit, incremental" row above stayed at the
clean-build md5.

title: Fix: track the AICore compiles' header dependencies
